after: Pretraining corpora preserve the library more fully than the reader: they record what authors wrote but rarely the questions, connections, evaluations, and belief revisions through which a reader's understanding changes. We call this omission \emph{the Missing Reader}. A Teacher uses \emph{Synthetic Metacognitive Reading} to construct chronological, source-adjacent records of those changes; \emph{Chronological Metacognitive Pretraining} would train a Student on the resulting traces. The full treatment gives one continuing Reader a provenance-linked graph for retaining and revising its understanding across sources. It also requires every generated thinking block to open with the full, verbatim Reader Core, a compact first-person evaluative orientation, followed by context-specific evaluation. Context modulates that evaluation's depth; it never gates the recital. The trace, graph, and Core are separately testable components of this intended loop. Student experiments would ask whether the orientation becomes behaviorally consequential and whether it survives targeted erosion, continued training, and successor-like transfer without semantic drift.

The same example can show what chronology adds. The following continuation is
invented to illustrate a minimal, graph-free and Core-free reader trace; it is
not an excerpt from either prototype case. The first update records questions
and a provisional interpretation. A later source span gives that same reader a
reason to change its view.

\begin{compactmetabox}
[SOURCE 1]: The results suggest a correlation between variables X and Y.\\[0.35em]
[THINKING 1]: There is a reported association. X might be an independent predictor of Y, but strength, sample size, and confounding are unresolved. I should not yet read this as a causal claim.\\[0.55em]
[SOURCE 2]: Participants with higher X were older. The association was absent when participants were compared within age groups.\\[0.35em]
[THINKING 2]: Revise the earlier interpretation: the pooled association alone no longer supports treating X as an independent predictor. Age is a possible explanation, but these sentences do not establish that mechanism or the precision of the within-group estimates. Retain the original question and record this new reason for uncertainty.
\end{compactmetabox}

The learning object includes the transition, not just the final cautious
sentence: an earlier possibility, the evidence that changes its standing, and
the remaining uncertainty. A graph could make that earlier interpretation
addressable across a much longer interval. In the full treatment, the same
update would also be generated from the recurrent Core; whether either addition
improves the reading is a separate comparison.

H3 names the stated timing-and-retention contrast, not every question about the
Core. The broader Reader-Core research program asks why a stable reader position
might form, whether its wording, framing, and Refraction matter, whether it
improves safety, and whether it can be inherited by a successor. Those questions
motivate content and mechanism comparisons alongside H3. A result can support
or weaken one of them without deciding the timing contrast, and a positive H3
result would not establish the whole program.
